verified_facts.text: The hotel is in the former First National Bank Tower, which has anchored Dallas's Main Street District since 1965.
verified_facts.excerpt: Since 1965, the First National Bank Tower has anchored the Main Street District with a modern, global vision of Dallas.

verified_facts.text: The building's exterior was designed in the 1960s by architect George Dahl.
verified_facts.excerpt: The exterior was designed in the ‘60s by George Dahl, the architect behind some of Dallas’s most iconic buildings, including much of Fair Park and the Neimans flagship.

verified_facts.text: The National was once the tallest building west of the Mississippi.
verified_facts.excerpt: Once the tallest building west of the Mississippi, the National sat vacant for nearly a decade before developers launched a complete renovation.

verified_facts.text: Thompson Dallas is the first Thompson hotel in Texas and takes up about half the building, with offices and residences on the upper floors.
verified_facts.excerpt: The first Thompson outpost in Texas now takes up about half the building, with office spaces and residences on the upper floors.

verified_facts.text: Original materials such as the ninth floor's travertine walls were restored.
verified_facts.excerpt: much of the building’s original materials, like the ninth floor’s travertine walls, were restored.

verified_facts.text: The National also houses Samuel Lynne Galleries, showing contemporary art, and Lucchese, known for handcrafted Western style.
verified_facts.excerpt: Thompson Dallas calls The National home alongside Samuel Lynne Galleries, showcasing contemporary art, and Lucchese, carrying forward a legacy of handcrafted Western style.

verified_facts.text: Rooms are designed with mid-century flair, walnut woods and brass touches.
verified_facts.excerpt: Designed with original mid-century flair, walnut woods and brass touches

verified_facts.text: Room decor brings in 1960s-style furniture, light fixtures and brass accents, styled with cow print and leather.
verified_facts.excerpt: Mad Men–meets–urban–cowboy decor brings in 1960s-style furniture, light fixtures, and brass accents, all styled with cow print and leather.

verified_facts.text: Beds have a fold-out reading light built into the headboard.
verified_facts.excerpt: a fold out reading light built into the headboard so you can stay up late without blinding the person next to you

verified_facts.text: Rooms stock D.S. & Durga bath products.
verified_facts.excerpt: D.S. & Durga bath products

verified_facts.text: The Penthouse Suite has a fireplace and a separate living room.
verified_facts.excerpt: Elevate your stay in our Penthouse Suite with a cozy fireplace, stellar cityscapes, a separate living room

verified_facts.text: Monarch, on the 49th floor, is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant.
verified_facts.excerpt: Located on the 49th floor, Monarch is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant

verified_facts.text: Monarch was imagined by chef Danny Grant and team.
verified_facts.excerpt: Monarch is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant imagined by two Michelin Star chefs, Danny Grant and team.

verified_facts.text: Monarch is independently managed by Maple Hospitality Group.
verified_facts.excerpt: Monarch is independently managed by Maple Hospitality Group.

verified_facts.text: Catbird is a restaurant and lounge with a rooftop terrace overlooking downtown Dallas.
verified_facts.excerpt: Catbird is a jewel box restaurant and lounge with a rooftop terrace overlooking downtown Dallas.

verified_facts.text: Catbird's terrace has a greenery-covered pergola.
verified_facts.excerpt: the greenery-covered pergola on the expansive terrace offers a much more tropical vibe

verified_facts.text: Little Daisy is a Franco-American bistro.
verified_facts.excerpt: Little Daisy is a Franco-American bistro in downtown Dallas, where European flair meets American fare.

verified_facts.text: The rooftop pool is on the ninth floor.
verified_facts.excerpt: Relax at our resort-style rooftop pool on the 9th floor!

verified_facts.text: The rooftop pool has rentable private cabanas with TVs.
verified_facts.excerpt: rent a private cabana with TVs and luxury lounge seating

verified_facts.text: The rooftop pool is infinity-edge.
verified_facts.excerpt: Set beside Thompson Dallas’ rooftop infinity-edge pool

verified_facts.text: The spa terrace overlooking downtown has infrared saunas and hot and cold plunge pools.
verified_facts.excerpt: like the infrared saunas and hot and cold plunge pools on the spa’s terrace overlooking downtown

verified_facts.text: The spa has a blow dry bar and a nail salon.
verified_facts.excerpt: there’s also a blow dry bar and nail salon in the spa, too.

verified_facts.text: The hotel has some two acres of outdoor space.
verified_facts.excerpt: A huge perk here is the outdoor space, some two acres of it.

verified_facts.text: A daily destination fee, subject to change, applies to each room.
verified_facts.excerpt: A daily destination fee of $35.00 (subject to change) is applied to each room of your stay

verified_facts.text: Dogs are welcome at no additional charge for stays under 30 nights.
verified_facts.excerpt: We welcome dogs at no additional charge for stays less than 30 nights.

verified_facts.text: Akard Station and St. Paul Station on the DART light rail are both within walking distance.
verified_facts.excerpt: nearby stations including Akard Station and St. Paul Station, both within walking distance of Thompson Dallas.

verified_facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler advises having a rental car to explore beyond a four-block radius.
verified_facts.excerpt: be sure to have a rental car if you plan on exploring beyond a four-block radius

verified_facts.text: The DART light rail can sometimes be faintly heard from the station below.
verified_facts.excerpt: sometimes I could faintly hear the DART light rail from the station below

Up on the 49th floor, not far from the penthouses, the National’s two restaurants are both helmed by Michelin-star Chef Danny Grant.
